speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. text: Based on your recent camping trip and the history of a self-resolving knee pain, I am highly suspicious of Lyme disease causing this wrist arthritis. However, your sexual activity also requires us to rule out Disseminated Gonococcal Infection. speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (DGI).

The combination of sexually active status, asymmetric migratory polyarthralgia (knee then wrist), fever, and the classic presentation of a pustular rash on the extremities is pathognomonic for DGI. Lyme disease is unlikely given the lack of a described annular rash (erythema migrans) and the specific sexual history. We do not need further testing to proceed with empiric treatment for gonococcal septic arthritis.
